answer.rationale: Write-path p99 at 5x began after the only new change (release ~2h ago) while daily settlement peak is a known load pattern, so the release is the leading hypothesis. memory_b1 is the closest prior: rollback cleared a post-release checkout failure without losing customer work. memory_b5 is the main alternative (primary overloaded by reads/reports, writes recover if those move to replicas) and must be checked before committing, because writes are heavy now and replica routing would not drop customer writes. Reject enable_circuit_breaker: memory_b4 is fail-fast on a dependency and would shed writes, which violates the objective. add_capacity (b3) and failover are weaker: daily peak should already be sized, and there is no regional signal. Scale stays below broad_rollout because cause is not proven and settlement is in-flight; intervening on the write path at peak is flagged as downstream value risk. Uncertainty preserved: timing is correlative, not causal.
